criterion: The map fills the home surface as its subject, with the search field, the welcome card and the control rail reading as quiet furniture above.
evaluation_rule: The home surface shows a full-viewport map with a search field, a dismissible welcome card and a vertical rail of map controls floating over it. Yes if the map occupies the viewport and the overlaid panels read as secondary furniture. No if a panel, a hero band or a marketing composition takes the visual lead away from the map.

criterion: A mapper reading a conflict refusal learns from that message which feature clashed.
evaluation_rule: When an upload loses a version race the mapper is shown a refusal. Yes if that message identifies the clashing feature and states both the version the mapper held and the version now stored. No if the message is generic, names no feature, or omits either version.

criterion: The editor warning about a self-crossing way can be dismissed, leaving the upload free to proceed.
evaluation_rule: The editor raises soft warnings before an upload. Yes if a warning can be dismissed and the upload then completes. No if a warning blocks the upload, or if a way that crosses itself raises nothing at all.

criterion: A visitor who has signed out reads the map, searches the dataset and reaches the diary.
evaluation_rule: Reading is open to everyone here. Yes if the map, the search and the diary are all usable with no account and no sign-in prompt interrupts them. No if any read surface demands an account or shows a sign-in wall.

criterion: The changeset stream sits tight enough that a full page of history is read in one screen.
evaluation_rule: This product is operational at its data surfaces and calmer on the reading pages. Yes if the history rows are dense enough to read a whole page at once while the reading pages carry noticeably more space. No if both are set at one density, or if the history surface is airy enough to force scrolling through a short list.

criterion: The revert confirmation names what a revert will undo before the revert is applied.
evaluation_rule: A revert is destructive, so it confirms first. Yes if the confirmation names the changeset being undone and the mapper must accept it before anything changes. No if a revert applies straight from one click, or if the confirmation names nothing in particular.

criterion: The colour reserved for destroying something appears on the revert confirmation alone.
evaluation_rule: One colour in this product means something has gone wrong or will be destroyed. Yes if that colour appears on the revert confirmation while every ordinary navigation control, save control and informational badge wears a different one. No if the same colour is reused decoratively elsewhere.

criterion: The green reserved for editing the world appears on the edit control in the header.
evaluation_rule: A soft green marks where a mapper may change the world. Yes if the edit control and the brand mark wear it while every other control wears something else. No if the green spreads to secondary buttons, links or headings.

criterion: On the map home the marker showing a viewer position sends out one soft expanding ripple.
evaluation_rule: The locate control drops a marker for the position of the person viewing. Yes if that marker emits an expanding, fading ripple and every other element in the product moves less than it does. No if the marker is static, or if some other animation is more prominent.

criterion: Every icon-only control in the map rail carries a name a screen reader announces.
evaluation_rule: The rail holds zoom in, zoom out, locate, layers, share and help as icon-only controls. Yes if each exposes a text alternative naming what it does. No if any one of them is an unlabelled glyph.

criterion: At a phone width the map home header collapses its navigation behind one toggle that opens a stacked menu.
evaluation_rule: Narrow the viewport to a phone width. Yes if the navigation sits behind a single toggle, the search and welcome panels span the width, and the help cards stack into one column. No if the desktop navigation persists, if a panel keeps a fixed narrow width, or if the help grid keeps more than one column.
